what_is_wrong: Discard never performs the status transition. It only stamps discarded_at and leaves status=DRAFT. Consequences proven live: (1) the run stays in the DRAFT list, (2) the status=DISCARDED filter returns 0 rows so a discarded run is unfindable as discarded, and (3) because confirm only guards on status != 'DRAFT' and never looks at discarded_at, a discarded run can still be recalculated AND confirmed â€” writing real payslips for a run the accountant deliberately threw away. The resulting row is self-contradictory: discarded_at set AND status=PROCESSED.
evidence:
POST /api/v1/payroll/runs/aa40bd00-8230-4b21-92c6-ca065051a8bf/discard
-> 200 {"id":"aa40bd00-...","status":"DRAFT","discarded_at":"2026-08-26T07:02:29.229051"}

GET /api/v1/payroll/runs/aa40bd00-8230-4b21-92c6-ca065051a8bf
-> 200  status=DRAFT  discarded_at=2026-08-26T07:02:29.229051

GET /api/v1/payroll/runs?status=DISCARDED
-> 200 []            (n=0; the discarded run is absent)
GET /api/v1/payroll/runs?status=DRAFT
-> 200 [... 'aa40bd00-8230-4b21-92c6-ca065051a8bf' ...]   (still listed as DRAFT)

POST /api/v1/payroll/runs/aa40bd00-8230-4b21-92c6-ca065051a8bf/recalculate
-> 200 (status DRAFT)   -- a discarded run still recalculates

POST /api/v1/payroll/runs/aa40bd00-8230-4b21-92c6-ca065051a8bf/confirm
-> 200 status now PROCESSED, discarded_at still 2026-08-26T07:02:29.229051, net 18354.84

GET /api/v1/payroll/payslips?period_month=9
-> 2 payslips written by the DISCARDED run:
   0c84b774-62a3-4d2b-8edd-f0c1f3f88420 Suresh Iyer net 7241.94 PROCESSED
   a1abc89b-496f-4bc3-ad9c-900f90160207 Kavya Nair  net 11112.90 PROCESSED
suspected_cause: app/api/v1/payroll_runs.py:730 â€” sets run.discarded_at but never run.status = "DISCARDED"; and app/api/v1/payroll_runs.py:747 â€” confirm guards only on `if run.status != "DRAFT"`, ignoring discarded_at

status_observed: 200 OK â€” payslip persisted with net_pay 99999.00 against total_earnings 32000.00 / total_deductions 26000.00 (should be 6000.00); a later call persisted an entirely negative payslip
what_is_wrong: MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT reissue writes manual_gross_pay / manual_total_earnings / manual_total_deductions / manual_net_pay into the payslip as four independent fields with no cross-field reconciliation and no sign check. The API will happily store a legally-issued payslip whose stated net pay bears no relation to its own earnings and deductions, and will store negative money. This is the corrective path for an already-wrong payslip, so it is the last place that should skip validation.
suspected_cause: app/api/v1/payslips.py:485-493 â€” four independent `if body.manual_* is not None: payslip.<field> = ...` assignments, no validation between them
short_summary: Manual reissue accepts incoherent and negative money

status_observed: 200 OK â€” returns the identical 110 rows for every hour_status value, including nonsense values
what_is_wrong: The `hour_status` query parameter is inert because the loop that builds the rows reassigns the same variable name. By the time the filter runs, `hour_status` holds the status computed for the LAST employee in the loop, not the caller's argument. So the endpoint filters by an arbitrary data-dependent value instead of the requested one. Asking for hour_status=Met returns 110 rows all labelled "Short â€” payroll impact". The bug is data-dependent, not merely a no-op: had the last employee resolved to "Met", a caller asking for "Short â€” payroll impact" would have received only Met rows. The sibling endpoint monthly-summary implements the identical filter correctly using a separate local (`resolved_status`), and does filter properly (Met=4, impact=110).
evidence:
GET /api/v1/payroll/attendance/payroll-impact?period_month=7&period_year=2028
-> 200, 110 rows

hour_status='Met'                     -> 110 rows, identical to unfiltered: True
hour_status='Short â€” compensable'     -> 110 rows, identical to unfiltered: True
hour_status='Short â€” payroll impact'  -> 110 rows, identical to unfiltered: True
hour_status='TOTALLY BOGUS VALUE'     -> 110 rows, identical to unfiltered: True

Every returned row carries "status": "Short â€” payroll impact", so hour_status=Met is demonstrably wrong.

Contrast, same period, the sibling endpoint which is correct:
GET /api/v1/payroll/attendance/monthly-summary?period_month=7&period_year=2028&hour_status=Met -> 4 rows
GET ...&hour_status=Short%20â€”%20payroll%20impact -> 110 rows
GET ...&hour_status=Bananas -> 0 rows
suspected_cause: app/api/v1/attendance_reconciliation.py:460/463/466 reassign the `hour_status` parameter inside the per-employee loop; :475-476 then filter on that clobbered value (and :481 reports it as filters_applied in the export header)
short_summary: hour_status param shadowed by loop variable, filters wrong

status_observed: 500 {"detail": "Internal server error"} for every database-rejected write, including a plain foreign-key violation
what_is_wrong: The endpoint has a try/except DBAPIError specifically to convert database rejections into client errors, but the parent row is written by `await db.flush()` on the line BEFORE the try block. Every constraint violation on the adjustment row itself therefore escapes the handler and surfaces as an unhandled 500 instead of the intended 409/422 â€” including an out-of-enum adjustment_type or applies_to_mode (neither of which is enumerated in the OpenAPI schema, both declared as plain `string`, so a client cannot know the legal values), an over-length label, and a non-existent employee_id FK. Writes do roll back cleanly â€” no orphan rows were left â€” so this is a validation/robustness defect, not data corruption.
suspected_cause: app/api/v1/adhoc_adjustments.py:156 â€” `await db.flush()` sits outside the try/except DBAPIError at :163-167 that exists to call _as_client_error
short_summary: db.flush() outside try; all DB rejections 500 instead of 409

status_observed: 500 {"detail": "Internal server error"} for any period_month outside 1..12
what_is_wrong: period_month is declared as a bare required integer with no minimum/maximum in the OpenAPI schema, and the value flows straight into `date(period_year, period_month, 1)`, which raises ValueError: month must be in 1..12. The exception is unhandled, producing a 500 instead of a 422. This affects all four attendance endpoints plus POST /payroll/runs, which share resolve_pay_period().

GET /api/v1/payroll/attendance/monthly-summary?period_month=99&period_year=2028 -> 500

Same for every sibling (months 0, 13, 99, -1 all 500):

And on the write path:

status_observed: 200 OK â€” employee_id filter returns 3 of the 6 adjustments that actually target that employee
what_is_wrong: The employee_id filter matches only the adjustments table's own employee_id column, which is populated exclusively for applies_to_mode=SINGLE_EMPLOYEE and left NULL for MULTIPLE_EMPLOYEES and ALL_ACTIVE_EMPLOYEES. Adjustments that genuinely target an employee through the adhoc_adjustment_employees join table are therefore silently omitted. An accountant filtering "show me everything hitting this employee's payslip" will not see a company-wide bonus or a multi-employee recovery that is in fact deducted from that person's pay.
